+#Requires -Version 5.1
+
+# Runs scripts/install.ps1 for real against GitHub Releases and checks what it
+# leaves behind. It rewrites the user PATH and installs binaries under the
+# profile, so it refuses to run anywhere but GitHub Actions; the raw user PATH
+# and its value kind are restored at the end regardless.
+#
+# Phases, each asserting before the next:
+#   1. stable install through the documented `irm | iex` shape
+#   2. reinstall while entire.exe is running, then again after it exits
+#   3. nightly install into a second directory, alongside the first
+
+# Phase 1 runs the installer through the documented `irm | iex` shape, which
+# is the point of that phase.
+[Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSAvoidUsingInvokeExpression', '', Justification = 'Phase 1 exercises the documented irm | iex shape')]
+param()
+
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+
+if ($env:CI -ne 'true' -or $env:GITHUB_ACTIONS -ne 'true') {
+    throw 'scripts/test/e2e.ps1 installs into the user profile and rewrites the user PATH; it runs only in GitHub Actions CI.'
+}
+
+$installerPath = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot) 'install.ps1'
+# Dot-sourcing loads the functions without installing.
+. $installerPath
+
+function Assert-Equal {
+    param([string] $Phase, [string] $What, $Expected, $Actual)
+    if (-not [object]::Equals($Expected, $Actual)) {
+        throw "[$Phase] $What`n  expected: $Expected`n  actual:   $Actual"
+    }
+}
+
+function Assert-True {
+    param([string] $Phase, [string] $What, [bool] $Condition)
+    if (-not $Condition) {
+        throw "[$Phase] $What"
+    }
+}
+
+function Get-PathEntry {
+    param([AllowNull()] [string] $Value)
+    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($Value)) {
+        return @()
+    }
+    return @($Value -split ';')
+}
+
+function Get-UserPathKind {
+    $key = (Get-Item -LiteralPath 'HKCU:').OpenSubKey('Environment')
+    if ($null -eq $key -or $null -eq $key.GetValue('Path', $null, [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueOptions]::DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames)) {
+        return $null
+    }
+    return $key.GetValueKind('Path')
+}
+
+# The kind Write-UserEnvironmentValue promises: ExpandString when the value
+# contains %, otherwise whatever the value had before, String if it did not
+# exist.
+function Get-ExpectedKind {
+    param([string] $NewValue, $PreviousKind)
+    if ($NewValue.Contains('%')) {
+        return [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueKind]::ExpandString
+    }
+    if ($null -ne $PreviousKind) {
+        return $PreviousKind
+    }
+    return [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueKind]::String
+}
+
+# The machine PATH as stored, for the phase that plants a copy on it.
+function Get-MachinePathKey {
+    (Get-Item -LiteralPath 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager').OpenSubKey('Environment', $true)
+}
+
+function Get-MachinePath {
+    (Get-MachinePathKey).GetValue('Path', $null, [Microsoft.Win32.RegistryValueOptions]::DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames)
+}
+
+# Runs $Body in a child of the same shell, so each CI leg tests its own host.
+function Invoke-ChildShell {
+    param([string] $Body)
+    $shell = (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path
+    @(& $shell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command $Body 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" })
+}
+
+function Invoke-Installer {
+    # A hashtable splat binds by name; an array splat would bind positionally.
+    param([hashtable] $Arguments = @{})
+    $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $installerPath))
+    # Write-Host is the information stream; merge it so the report can be asserted.
+    & $installer @Arguments 6>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" }
+}
+
+function Get-EntireVersion {
+    param([string] $Phase, [string] $Directory)
+    $output = & (Join-Path $Directory 'entire.exe') version 2>&1 | Out-String
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $Phase -What 'entire.exe version exit code' -Expected 0 -Actual $LASTEXITCODE
+    return $output.Trim()
+}
+
+$snapshot = Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path'
+$snapshotKind = Get-UserPathKind
+$snapshotEntries = Get-PathEntry $snapshot
+# This process's PATH before any install: what a terminal opened before the
+# first install would inherit.
+$processPathBefore = $env:Path
+$machineSnapshot = Get-MachinePath
+$machineSnapshotKind = (Get-MachinePathKey).GetValueKind('Path')
+$stubDir = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'entire-machine-stub'
+$stableDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.local\bin'
+$nightlyDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'entire-nightly'
+$running = $null
+
+try {
+    # ---- Phase 1: stable through irm | iex --------------------------------
+    $phase = 'phase 1: stable via iex'
+    Write-Host "==> $phase"
+    Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $installerPath | Invoke-Expression
+
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'entire.exe installed' -Condition (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $stableDir 'entire.exe') -PathType Leaf)
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'git-remote-entire.exe installed' -Condition (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $stableDir 'git-remote-entire.exe') -PathType Leaf)
+
+    $afterStable = Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path'
+    $entries = Get-PathEntry $afterStable
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'first raw PATH entry' -Expected $stableDir -Actual $entries[0]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'remaining raw PATH entries' -Expected ($snapshotEntries -join ';') -Actual (($entries | Select-Object -Skip 1) -join ';')
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'raw PATH value kind' -Expected (Get-ExpectedKind -NewValue $afterStable -PreviousKind $snapshotKind) -Actual (Get-UserPathKind)
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'first in-process $env:Path entry' -Expected $stableDir -Actual ((Get-PathEntry $env:Path)[0])
+    $stableVersion = Get-EntireVersion -Phase $phase -Directory $stableDir
+    Write-Host "    stable: $stableVersion"
+
+    # ---- Phase 2: reinstall while entire.exe is running -------------------
+    $phase = 'phase 2: reinstall while running'
+    Write-Host "==> $phase"
+    $startInfo = New-Object System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo
+    $startInfo.FileName = Join-Path $stableDir 'entire.exe'
+    $startInfo.Arguments = 'mcp'
+    $startInfo.UseShellExecute = $false
+    $startInfo.RedirectStandardInput = $true
+    $startInfo.RedirectStandardOutput = $true
+    # stdin is never written to or closed, so the MCP server waits on it.
+    $running = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::Start($startInfo)
+    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'entire mcp is still running' -Condition (-not $running.HasExited)
+
+    # A mapped executable image refuses to be opened for writing. Prove that
+    # without writing anything: if the open succeeds, the file is untouched
+    # and the precondition, not a later phase, is what fails.
+    $opened = $false
+    try {
+        $handle = [IO.File]::Open((Join-Path $stableDir 'entire.exe'), [IO.FileMode]::Open, [IO.FileAccess]::Write)
+        $handle.Dispose()
+        $opened = $true
+    }
+    catch {
+        $opened = $false
+    }
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'running entire.exe refuses a write handle (precondition)' -Condition (-not $opened)
+
+    Invoke-Installer | Out-Null
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'entire.exe.old left behind while the old image runs' -Condition (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $stableDir 'entire.exe.old') -PathType Leaf)
+    Get-EntireVersion -Phase $phase -Directory $stableDir | Out-Null
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'raw PATH after reinstall' -Expected $afterStable -Actual (Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path')
+
+    $running.Kill()
+    $running.WaitForExit()
+    $running = $null
+    Invoke-Installer | Out-Null
+    $stale = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $stableDir -Filter 'entire.exe*.old' -File)
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'stale .old files after the old image exited' -Expected 0 -Actual $stale.Count
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'raw PATH after the third install' -Expected $afterStable -Actual (Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path')
+
+    # ---- Phase 3: nightly into a second directory, from a stale shell ------
+    # The installer tells the user to restart the terminal between installs.
+    # A terminal opened before phase 1 wrote the registry has a PATH without
+    # the stable directory, so this install runs in a child given exactly that
+    # PATH; the stable copy must then be reported from the stored PATH alone.
+    $phase = 'phase 3: nightly to a custom dir from a stale shell'
+    Write-Host "==> $phase"
+    $childBody = @(
+        "`$env:Path = '$processPathBefore'"
+        "if (@(`$env:Path -split ';' | Where-Object { `$_ -eq '$stableDir' }).Count -eq 0) { 'PRECONDITION: stable dir absent from this shell' }"
+        "& ([scriptblock]::Create((Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath '$installerPath'))) -Channel nightly -InstallDir '$nightlyDir' 6>&1 | ForEach-Object { `"`$_`" }"
+    ) -join '; '
+    $reportLines = Invoke-ChildShell -Body $childBody
+    $report = $reportLines -join "`n"
+    # The assertions below judge this text; show it so a failure is diagnosable from the log.
+    Write-Host $report
+
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'child shell PATH lacked the stable dir (precondition)' -Condition ($reportLines -contains 'PRECONDITION: stable dir absent from this shell')
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'conflict warning printed' -Condition ($report -match '! WARNING: PATH conflict detected')
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'stored-PATH group printed' -Condition ($reportLines -contains '! Also on your saved PATH, not active in this shell:')
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'stable install named under the stored-PATH group' -Condition ($reportLines -contains "!   $(Join-Path $stableDir 'entire.exe')")
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'nightly install reported as taking priority' -Condition ($report -match 'The installed version takes priority')
+
+    $afterNightly = Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path'
+    $entries = Get-PathEntry $afterNightly
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'first raw PATH entry' -Expected $nightlyDir -Actual $entries[0]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'second raw PATH entry (stable, moved down, not removed)' -Expected $stableDir -Actual $entries[1]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'remaining raw PATH entries' -Expected ($snapshotEntries -join ';') -Actual (($entries | Select-Object -Skip 2) -join ';')
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'raw PATH value kind' -Expected (Get-ExpectedKind -NewValue $afterNightly -PreviousKind $snapshotKind) -Actual (Get-UserPathKind)
+    $nightlyVersion = Get-EntireVersion -Phase $phase -Directory $nightlyDir
+    Write-Host "    nightly: $nightlyVersion"
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'nightly binary reports a nightly version' -Condition ($nightlyVersion -match 'nightly')
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'nightly and stable versions differ' -Condition ($nightlyVersion -ne $stableVersion)
+
+    # ---- Phase 4: a copy on the machine-wide PATH ---------------------------
+    # Windows composes a new session as machine PATH then user PATH, so a copy
+    # in a machine-PATH directory outranks anything the installer writes; the
+    # report has a paragraph for that. The runner is elevated, so plant one.
+    $phase = 'phase 4: copy on the machine PATH'
+    Write-Host "==> $phase"
+    [IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($stubDir) | Out-Null
+    Copy-Item -LiteralPath $env:ComSpec -Destination (Join-Path $stubDir 'entire.exe')
+    (Get-MachinePathKey).SetValue('Path', "$machineSnapshot;$stubDir", $machineSnapshotKind)
+    $report = Invoke-Installer | Out-String
+    Write-Host $report
+
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'machine-PATH paragraph printed' -Condition ($report -match 'is on the machine-wide PATH')
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'machine-PATH copy named' -Condition ($report.Contains("$(Join-Path $stubDir 'entire.exe') is on the machine-wide PATH"))
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'install-over remedy names the machine-PATH directory' -Condition ($report.Contains("!   -InstallDir $stubDir"))
+    # Reinstalling stable puts its directory first again; the nightly entry
+    # moves down by one and nothing else changes.
+    $entries = Get-PathEntry (Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path')
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'first raw PATH entry' -Expected $stableDir -Actual $entries[0]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'second raw PATH entry' -Expected $nightlyDir -Actual $entries[1]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'remaining raw PATH entries' -Expected ($snapshotEntries -join ';') -Actual (($entries | Select-Object -Skip 2) -join ';')
+
+    Write-Host '==> all phases passed'
+}
+finally {
+    if ($null -ne $running -and -not $running.HasExited) {
+        $running.Kill()
+        $running.WaitForExit()
+    }
+    # The runner is ephemeral; restoring anyway records that this script
+    # knows it mutated shared state.
+    if ($null -ne $machineSnapshot) {
+        (Get-MachinePathKey).SetValue('Path', $machineSnapshot, $machineSnapshotKind)

+    $key = (Get-Item -LiteralPath 'HKCU:').CreateSubKey('Environment')

+        $key.DeleteValue('Path', $false)
+    }
+    else {
+        $key.SetValue('Path', $snapshot, $snapshotKind)

+# Installs what scripts/test/run.ps1 needs, for the current user, once on a
+# fresh machine. Safe to rerun: each step is skipped when already satisfied.
+#
+# Stock Windows PowerShell 5.1 ships PowerShellGet 1.0.0.1 without the NuGet
+# package provider, and its bootstrap is an interactive prompt that -Force
+# does not suppress, so a non-interactive Install-Module fails there until
+# the provider is installed. pwsh ships a modern PowerShellGet and skips that
+# step. GitHub's Windows runners preinstall both modules, so CI never runs this.
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+
+Write-Output "PowerShell $($PSVersionTable.PSVersion) ($($PSVersionTable.PSEdition))"
+
+if ($PSVersionTable.PSEdition -eq 'Desktop') {
+    $nuget = Get-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -ListAvailable -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+        Where-Object { $_.Version -ge [version]'2.8.5.201' } | Select-Object -First 1
+    if ($null -ne $nuget) {
+        Write-Output "NuGet provider $($nuget.Version) is already installed."
+    }
+    else {
+        Write-Output 'Installing the NuGet package provider...'
+        Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -MinimumVersion 2.8.5.201 -Scope CurrentUser -Force | Out-Null
+    }
+}
+
+# Pester 5.2 is the floor run.ps1 imports; 6.x is also known to work, so
+# there is no ceiling.
+$pester = Get-Module -Name Pester -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Version -ge [version]'5.2.0' } | Select-Object -First 1
+if ($null -ne $pester) {
+    Write-Output "Pester $($pester.Version) is already installed."
+}
+else {
+    Write-Output 'Installing Pester...'
+    Install-Module -Repository PSGallery -Scope CurrentUser -Force -Name Pester -MinimumVersion 5.2.0 -SkipPublisherCheck
+}
+
+$analyzer = Get-Module -Name PSScriptAnalyzer -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Version -ge [version]'1.17.1' } | Select-Object -First 1
+if ($null -ne $analyzer) {
+    Write-Output "PSScriptAnalyzer $($analyzer.Version) is already installed."
+}
+else {
+    Write-Output 'Installing PSScriptAnalyzer...'
+    Install-Module -Repository PSGallery -Scope CurrentUser -Force -Name PSScriptAnalyzer -MinimumVersion 1.17.1 -SkipPublisherCheck
+}
+
+Write-Output 'Ready: run scripts/test/run.ps1 or `mise run test:ps1`.'"},{"sha":"471ad6dec9b398a5514dfe0d48a47f5a27181217","filename":"scripts/test/run.ps1","status":"added","additions":40,"deletions":0,"changes":40,"blob_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/b36fdf7254305b78ae61260921b848888b6646ec/scripts%2Ftest%2Frun.ps1","raw_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/raw/b36fdf7254305b78ae61260921b848888b6646ec/scripts%2Ftest%2Frun.ps1","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/entireio/cli/contents/scripts%2Ftest%2Frun.ps1?ref=b36fdf7254305b78ae61260921b848888b6646ec","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+#Requires -Version 5.1
+
+# Runs the PowerShell test suite under scripts/test. CI (both Windows
+# PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh) and `mise run test:ps1` call this, so Pester
+# configuration lives here once. On a fresh machine run scripts/test/init.ps1
+# first; it installs Pester, PSScriptAnalyzer and, on Windows PowerShell 5.1,
+# the NuGet provider they need.
+#
+# The module floors are enforced with Import-Module rather than `#Requires
+# -Modules`: under `pwsh -File`, a `#Requires -Modules` line makes the script's
+# `exit` code come back as 0, so a failing suite would pass CI. Import-Module
+# also selects the highest satisfying version, which matters on Windows where
+# the OS-bundled Pester 3.4.0 sits next to the modern one.
+#
+# The exit code keys on the run's overall Result, not on FailedCount: a test
+# file that fails to parse, or a BeforeAll that throws, leaves FailedCount at
+# 0 (the tests never existed to fail) while Result is Failed.
+#
+# -Path exists so a test can run this against a directory of its own.
+param([string] $Path = $PSScriptRoot)
+
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+Import-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.2.0
+Import-Module PSScriptAnalyzer -MinimumVersion 1.17.1
+
+$pesterConfig = New-PesterConfiguration -Hashtable @{
+    Run    = @{
+        Path     = $Path
+        PassThru = $true
+    }
+    Output = @{
+        Verbosity = 'Detailed'
+    }
+}
+
+$result = Invoke-Pester -Configuration $pesterConfig
+if ($result.Result -ne 'Passed') {
+    exit 1
+}
+exit 0"}]}

+    $afterNightly = Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path'
+    $entries = Get-PathEntry $afterNightly
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'first raw PATH entry' -Expected $nightlyDir -Actual $entries[0]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'second raw PATH entry (stable, moved down, not removed)' -Expected $stableDir -Actual $entries[1]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'remaining raw PATH entries' -Expected ($snapshotEntries -join ';') -Actual (($entries | Select-Object -Skip 2) -join ';')
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'raw PATH value kind' -Expected (Get-ExpectedKind -NewValue $afterNightly -PreviousKind $snapshotKind) -Actual (Get-UserPathKind)
+    $nightlyVersion = Get-EntireVersion -Phase $phase -Directory $nightlyDir
+    Write-Host "    nightly: $nightlyVersion"
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'nightly binary reports a nightly version' -Condition ($nightlyVersion -match 'nightly')
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'nightly and stable versions differ' -Condition ($nightlyVersion -ne $stableVersion)
+
+    # ---- Phase 4: a copy on the machine-wide PATH ---------------------------
+    # Windows composes a new session as machine PATH then user PATH, so a copy
+    # in a machine-PATH directory outranks anything the installer writes; the
+    # report has a paragraph for that. The runner is elevated, so plant one.
+    $phase = 'phase 4: copy on the machine PATH'
+    Write-Host "==> $phase"
+    [IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($stubDir) | Out-Null
+    Copy-Item -LiteralPath $env:ComSpec -Destination (Join-Path $stubDir 'entire.exe')
+    (Get-MachinePathKey).SetValue('Path', "$machineSnapshot;$stubDir", $machineSnapshotKind)
+    $report = Invoke-Installer | Out-String
+    Write-Host $report
+
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'machine-PATH paragraph printed' -Condition ($report -match 'is on the machine-wide PATH')
+    Assert-True -Phase $phase -What 'machine-PATH copy named' -Condition ($report.Contains("$(Join-Path $stubDir 'entire.exe') is on the machine-wide PATH"))

+    # moves down by one and nothing else changes.
+    $entries = Get-PathEntry (Get-UserEnvironmentValue -Name 'Path')
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'first raw PATH entry' -Expected $stableDir -Actual $entries[0]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'second raw PATH entry' -Expected $nightlyDir -Actual $entries[1]
+    Assert-Equal -Phase $phase -What 'remaining raw PATH entries' -Expected ($snapshotEntries -join ';') -Actual (($entries | Select-Object -Skip 2) -join ';')
+

+#Requires -Version 5.1
+
+# Installs what scripts/test/run.ps1 needs, for the current user, once on a
+# fresh machine. Safe to rerun: each step is skipped when already satisfied.
+#
+# Stock Windows PowerShell 5.1 ships PowerShellGet 1.0.0.1 without the NuGet
+# package provider, and its bootstrap is an interactive prompt that -Force
+# does not suppress, so a non-interactive Install-Module fails there until
+# the provider is installed. pwsh ships a modern PowerShellGet and skips that
+# step. GitHub's Windows runners preinstall both modules, so CI never runs this.
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+
+Write-Output "PowerShell $($PSVersionTable.PSVersion) ($($PSVersionTable.PSEdition))"
+
+if ($PSVersionTable.PSEdition -eq 'Desktop') {
+    $nuget = Get-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -ListAvailable -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+        Where-Object { $_.Version -ge [version]'2.8.5.201' } | Select-Object -First 1
+    if ($null -ne $nuget) {
+        Write-Output "NuGet provider $($nuget.Version) is already installed."
+    }
+    else {
+        Write-Output 'Installing the NuGet package provider...'
+        Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -MinimumVersion 2.8.5.201 -Scope CurrentUser -Force | Out-Null
+    }
+}
+
+# Pester 5.2 is the floor run.ps1 imports; 6.x is also known to work, so
+# there is no ceiling.
+$pester = Get-Module -Name Pester -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Version -ge [version]'5.2.0' } | Select-Object -First 1
+if ($null -ne $pester) {
+    Write-Output "Pester $($pester.Version) is already installed."
+}
+else {
+    Write-Output 'Installing Pester...'
+    Install-Module -Repository PSGallery -Scope CurrentUser -Force -Name Pester -MinimumVersion 5.2.0 -SkipPublisherCheck
+}
+
+$analyzer = Get-Module -Name PSScriptAnalyzer -ListAvailable | Where-Object { $_.Version -ge [version]'1.17.1' } | Select-Object -First 1
+if ($null -ne $analyzer) {
+    Write-Output "PSScriptAnalyzer $($analyzer.Version) is already installed."
+}
+else {
+    Write-Output 'Installing PSScriptAnalyzer...'
+    Install-Module -Repository PSGallery -Scope CurrentUser -Force -Name PSScriptAnalyzer -MinimumVersion 1.17.1 -SkipPublisherCheck
+}
+
+Write-Output 'Ready: run scripts/test/run.ps1 or `mise run test:ps1`.'"},{"sha":"471ad6dec9b398a5514dfe0d48a47f5a27181217","filename":"scripts/test/run.ps1","status":"added","additions":40,"deletions":0,"changes":40,"blob_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/b36fdf7254305b78ae61260921b848888b6646ec/scripts%2Ftest%2Frun.ps1","raw_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/raw/b36fdf7254305b78ae61260921b848888b6646ec/scripts%2Ftest%2Frun.ps1","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/entireio/cli/contents/scripts%2Ftest%2Frun.ps1?ref=b36fdf7254305b78ae61260921b848888b6646ec","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+#Requires -Version 5.1
+
+# Runs the PowerShell test suite under scripts/test. CI (both Windows
+# PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh) and `mise run test:ps1` call this, so Pester
+# configuration lives here once. On a fresh machine run scripts/test/init.ps1
+# first; it installs Pester, PSScriptAnalyzer and, on Windows PowerShell 5.1,
+# the NuGet provider they need.
+#
+# The module floors are enforced with Import-Module rather than `#Requires
+# -Modules`: under `pwsh -File`, a `#Requires -Modules` line makes the script's
+# `exit` code come back as 0, so a failing suite would pass CI. Import-Module
+# also selects the highest satisfying version, which matters on Windows where
+# the OS-bundled Pester 3.4.0 sits next to the modern one.
+#
+# The exit code keys on the run's overall Result, not on FailedCount: a test
+# file that fails to parse, or a BeforeAll that throws, leaves FailedCount at
+# 0 (the tests never existed to fail) while Result is Failed.
+#
+# -Path exists so a test can run this against a directory of its own.
+param([string] $Path = $PSScriptRoot)
+
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+Import-Module Pester -MinimumVersion 5.2.0
+Import-Module PSScriptAnalyzer -MinimumVersion 1.17.1
+
+$pesterConfig = New-PesterConfiguration -Hashtable @{
+    Run    = @{
+        Path     = $Path
+        PassThru = $true
+    }
+    Output = @{
+        Verbosity = 'Detailed'
+    }
+}
+
+$result = Invoke-Pester -Configuration $pesterConfig
+if ($result.Result -ne 'Passed') {
+    exit 1
+}
+exit 0"}]}

      "textSnapshot": "Problem:\nThe CLI previously offered both synchronous and asynchronous mirror creation paths, selected by a setting (async_mirror_requests). ---
name: testing
description: >
  Local testing strategy and review guidance for meaningful tests, choosing unit vs integration vs end-to-end scope,
  avoiding production-only test seams and over-mocking, and keeping test helpers readable, especially in Go.
  Use when writing, changing, or reviewing tests; adding mocks or test helpers; deciding test scope; or when user mentions pfleidi:testing.
---

# Testing Guidance

## Core Principle

Tests should make changed behavior trustworthy without distorting production code. Prefer behavior and contracts over implementation details. Use the smallest scope that gives real confidence.

## Task Implementation

When `pfleidi:task-implement` owns a repository change, read and follow
[Task implementation TDD](references/task-implementation-tdd.md) before the
first repository edit. It is the mandatory policy for the unit-test baseline,
RED-first behavior changes, public-contract coverage, refactoring, and recovery
from code written before its test.

## Never Use Real Customer Data

**NEVER put real customer data in test cases.** No production records, real PII, real emails, real account/customer IDs, or scrubbed copies of live data — "anonymized" or "scrubbed" production data is still forbidden. Fabricate synthetic fixtures that exercise the same shape and edge cases. When reviewing, reject any test carrying real customer data outright.

## Choose Test Scope

- **Unit tests** - pure logic, parsing, validation, small components, and behavior with explicit dependencies that can be supplied naturally.
- **Integration tests** - real wiring, filesystem, config, databases, process boundaries, generated code, framework behavior, or cases where unit isolation would require awkward mocks or production-only seams.
- **End-to-end / smoke tests** - critical user or system flows across process or service boundaries. Keep these few, stable, and high value.

Cover changed behavior, important edge cases, and error paths. Do not chase line coverage with brittle tests that only exercise private structure.

## Preserve Test Layers

Unit, integration, and end-to-end suites are complementary layers with different costs. A fast unit suite may intentionally skip real wiring, config, databases, filesystems, generated code, or framework behavior when another suite owns that boundary. That is not incomplete unit testing; it is a useful split of responsibilities.

Before changing test scope, identify the missing confidence:

- If the gap is pure logic, parsing, validation, or small behavior with natural dependencies, add or adjust a unit test.
- If the gap is real wiring, config loading, filesystem/database behavior, generated code, process boundaries, or framework behavior, first check existing integration/e2e coverage. If coverage is missing, add a narrow integration/e2e test at that boundary.
- Preserve useful fast unit tests. Do not rewrite broad unit test suites into integration tests just to cover wiring. Convert a unit test only when its stated subject is wrong and an additive test at the right layer would not cover the gap.

## Avoid Production Test Seams

Do not add production code that exists only to make tests easier:

- Mutable function variables swapped in tests.
- Mutable package-wide settings changed by tests.
- Exported `Reset`, `Set`, or hook functions only used by tests.
- Global clocks, filesystems, HTTP clients, env readers, or command runners added only for unit tests.

If a test needs these, prefer dependency injection through existing construction paths, small typed interfaces around external effects, or a higher-scope integration test.

## Test Helpers

Helpers are useful when they make the test shorter and easier to understand. They are harmful when they hide the behavior being tested.

Use a helper when:

- It removes noisy setup or cleanup that is not the point of the test.
- Its name is domain-specific and explains what the caller gets.
- The test remains understandable without opening the helper.
- It preserves the important inputs, expected values, and assertions at the call site.

Inline the code instead when:

- The helper saves only a few lines but hides the arrange/act/assert flow.
- The reviewer must inspect the helper to know what behavior is asserted.
- The helper takes booleans, loose maps, or option bags that obscure intent.
- The helper embeds important defaults, expected values, or failure conditions.
- The helper is generic test plumbing with no domain meaning.

Prefer local helpers in the test file until reuse is clear. Moving helpers to shared test utilities raises the readability bar because future readers lose locality.

## Go-Specific Helper Rules

- Prefer table-driven tests or `t.Run` subtests when repeated cases share the same logic. Each table row should be a complete scenario with inputs, expected outputs, and a clear name.
- Keep expected values in the table row or test body. Do not hide them in helper defaults.
- Use `t.Run` names to identify cases, then keep failure messages focused on `got` vs `want`.
- If a helper can fail the test, accept `testing.TB` or `*testing.T` and call `t.Helper()` first so failures point to the caller.
- Use `t.Cleanup`, `t.TempDir`, and `t.Setenv` for resource setup when appropriate. Remember that process-wide changes such as environment or current-directory changes are not safe for parallel tests unless the testing API says so.
- Return concrete values from builders. Avoid global shared fixtures and mutable package state.
- Avoid generic assertion helpers unless they are clearly domain-specific. A direct `if got != want { t.Fatalf(...) }` is often more readable than an abstraction.

## Review Checklist

When writing or reviewing tests, flag:

- Changed behavior, edge cases, or error paths without meaningful coverage.
- Tests that prove private implementation details instead of behavior.
- Unit tests used where real wiring/config/filesystem/database/framework behavior is the confidence boundary.
- Review feedback that tries to replace useful unit tests with integration tests instead of adding a narrow integration/e2e test for a proven uncovered boundary.
- Helpers that force readers to leave the test to understand the scenario.
- Helpers that hide expected values, assertions, or important defaults.
- Production-only seams introduced to make tests pass.
- Broad mocks where an integration test would be simpler and more trustworthy.
- Real customer data in fixtures — production records, real PII, real IDs, or scrubbed copies of live data. Reject outright.

## Source Basis

This guidance is synthesized from Go's testing package documentation, Go's subtests guidance, and the Go table-driven tests wiki, plus local preferences about avoiding production-only test seams.

**NEVER put real customer data in test cases.** No production records, real PII, real emails, real account/customer IDs, or scrubbed copies of live data — "anonymized" or "scrubbed" production data is still forbidden. - **Integration tests** - real wiring, filesystem, config, databases, process boundaries, generated code, framework behavior, or cases where unit isolation would require awkward mocks or production-only seams.
- **End-to-end / smoke tests** - critical user or system flows across process or service boundaries. Keep these few, stable, and high value.

Unit, integration, and end-to-end suites are complementary layers with different costs. A fast unit suite may intentionally skip real wiring, config, databases, filesystems, generated code, or framework behavior when another suite owns that boundary. Before changing test scope, identify the missing confidence:

- If the gap is pure logic, parsing, validation, or small behavior with natural dependencies, add or adjust a unit test.

- Mutable function variables swapped in tests.
- Mutable package-wide settings changed by tests.

# Task Implementation TDD

Use this policy whenever `pfleidi:task-implement` owns a repository change.

## Combine Repository Guidance With This Policy

Read the applicable repository-local instructions and inspect its existing
tests before choosing commands, scope, fixtures, or helpers. Repository guidance
defines project mechanics such as test targets, setup, suite boundaries, and
established conventions. The principles in this policy remain mandatory: local
mechanics do not waive RED-first sequencing, meaningful public-contract
coverage, or the rules against brittle tests and production-only seams. When a
repository requirement genuinely cannot be satisfied together with these
principles, stop before editing and ask the user to resolve the conflict.

## Establish The Unit Baseline

Before changing a test or production file, run the repository's documented full
unit-test suite once. Do not include integration or end-to-end suites in this
default baseline; they usually have different setup and runtime costs. If no
full unit command exists or it cannot run locally, use the broadest available
unit command and state the limitation.

Record existing failures without fixing unrelated code. Continue only when
focused tests for the area being changed are independently green. If a baseline
failure overlaps that area and obscures new regressions, stop and ask how to
proceed.

## Change Behavior RED First

Use one focused red-green-refactor cycle for each behavior slice:

1. Identify the observable behavior that will change and the smallest test
   boundary that can prove it.
2. Write or change one meaningful test, run its focused command, and confirm it
   fails because the behavior is missing or incorrect—not because of a typo,
   broken fixture, or unrelated error.
3. Make the smallest production change that satisfies the test, then rerun the
   same focused command until it passes.
4. Refactor only while green. At the completed slice boundary, run the
   containing package or component checks and any distinct lint or build check
   required by the repository workflow.

For a bug fix, reproduce the bug with the failing test before fixing it. Add
separate RED cases for material edge cases or failure paths; do not combine
unrelated behavior merely to reduce the number of cycles.

Every public function or method added or behaviorally changed by the task must
have meaningful coverage of its public contract. A higher-level test counts
when it actually exercises that API and asserts its observable result; a
one-test-per-symbol layout is not required. Private helpers stay private and are
covered through public behavior rather than direct tests. Do not introduce
mocks, interfaces, or production-only seams merely to manufacture a unit test.

## Recover From Skipped RED

If the agent writes production code before observing the expected RED, discard
only those uncommitted agent-authored production edits and restart the slice
from the test. Do not keep or adapt them as reference. This recovery is part of
the authorized implementation workflow and needs no additional approval. If
the premature code is committed or mixed with pre-existing work, stop instead
of rewriting history or discarding someone else's changes.

| Rationalization | Required response |
| --- | --- |
| “It is obvious or only a few lines.” | Discard the premature production edit and begin with RED. |
| “It already works manually.” | Manual success does not prove that the test detects the missing behavior. |
| “The deadline makes test-after equivalent.” | Schedule pressure does not change test order. |
| “The full suite passed in CI.” | Run the current local unit baseline before editing. |

## Refactoring And Pre-Existing Code

A refactor changes internal structure without changing externally observable
behavior or contracts. Establish that the narrow existing behavior tests pass,
make the refactor in small steps, and keep them green. Add a characterization
test first when an important observable contract is uncovered, but do not
invent a failing assertion for behavior that should remain unchanged. If a
slice changes behavior or a public contract, it is not a refactor; split out
that change and use the RED-first cycle.

Treat implementation already present when the task starts as existing work.
Preserve it and add the smallest meaningful regression coverage. Before
accepting that test, observe the expected RED against a safe pre-change revision
or a focused reversible mutation, then restore the inherited implementation and
observe GREEN. Never discard or rewrite someone else's work to manufacture RED.
If no safe method can demonstrate the failure, stop and ask whether to accept
coverage whose regression sensitivity was not observed; do not call it verified
TDD.

If changed behavior has no meaningful automated test boundary, do not add a
ceremonial test. Identify the closest executable validation and obtain the
user's explicit agreement to the coverage limitation before implementation or
commit.

## Complete The Test Cycle

During red-green iteration, run only the focused test needed for feedback.
Broaden verification once at the completed slice boundary according to the
repository's verification rules. Before presenting the implementation as
code-ready, rerun the same full unit-test suite used for the baseline. A clean
baseline must remain clean; otherwise compare results and reject new failures.

Run integration or end-to-end suites locally only when the task's exit criteria,
the changed confidence boundary, or an explicit repository requirement calls
for them and their prerequisites are available. An unrelated failure is
evidence to report, not authority to expand the task and fix unrelated code.

## Red Flags

- Production code exists before the expected RED.
- A test passes the first time when it should prove new or incorrect behavior.
- A behavior change is labeled a refactor to avoid RED.
- Public behavior is untested while private helpers have direct tests.
- A remote CI result substitutes for the current local unit baseline.
- Unrelated baseline failures become unapproved repair work.

Stop and apply the relevant recovery or conflict rule before continuing.
